status_note: A summary written for ELI Legal, in its own words. It is not the text of the instrument and has not been validated by a qualified lawyer. Check the official text before relying on any statement in it.
title: ABA Formal Opinion 512: generative artificial intelligence tools
instrument: American Bar Association Standing Committee on Ethics and Professional Responsibility, Formal Opinion 512 (29 July 2024)
description: How the Model Rules of Professional Conduct apply to a lawyer's use of generative AI. State rules govern; check yours.

requirements.title: Competence
requirements.text: The lawyer understands the capacities and limits of the tool and reviews its output to the standard competence requires.
requirements.statement: I understand what this tool checks and does not check, and I have reviewed its output to the standard my duty of competence requires.

requirements.title: Confidentiality
requirements.text: Client information is protected; informed consent may be needed before it is put into a tool that could disclose it. This system sends nothing off the machine.

requirements.title: Communication with the client
requirements.text: The client is told about the use of generative AI where it is relevant to decisions about the representation.

requirements.title: Candour to the tribunal
requirements.text: No false statement of law or fact is made to a tribunal.
requirements.statement: I will not put any statement of law or fact from this work before a tribunal without verifying it myself.

requirements.title: Supervision
requirements.text: Supervising lawyers make reasonable efforts to ensure others' use of the tool complies with the rules.

requirements.title: Fees
requirements.text: Fees for AI-assisted work are reasonable.
